properties.statement: [BL-197] Two served descriptions describe a world that has changed, and both mislead in the direction of "do it the old way"
properties.value: {"evidence": "*Same field report, 2026-08-03/04.* (a) claim_region's own description still says the design *\"lives as a file in each person's checkout with no shared server to hold a lock\"*. Since --shared shipped there IS a shared server and every session attaches to it, so the tool's description now argues against what the fleet's protocol binds; the worker who hit it knew better, the next one will read it as current. It should describe advisory claims under the shared server and treat the file plus merge-driver path as the cross-clone case rather than the default. (b) import_graph warns honestly that a hand-authored document *\"had no stamp\"* and that provenance and the upgrade-direction check therefore cannot be run \u2014 but nothing says whether a hand-authored document is ALLOWED to claim one, and the stamp's minimal shape is discoverable only by exporting a graph and reading the result. Every adopt pass \u2014 the exact workflow that produces hand-authored documents \u2014 silently forfeits the check you most want on the day someone imports an old document into a newer binary. Fix: either accept a minimal {reflow2_version, schema_version} stamp and say so in the warning, or state plainly that hand-authored documents cannot be stamped and the check is unavailable to them. Related, known, still unactioned: this repo's own .mcp.json does not pass --shared (it is [\"--graph-path\", \"./.reflow2/graph\"] only) while every config reflow2_init.py generates does \u2014 the sole reason the stale-server export replay is hand-rolled at every release cut. Size S", "origin": "Migrated from docs/backlog.md BL-197 on 2026-08-07 (epoch:backlog-retired). Size estimate carried from the row: S."}
